questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to improve my German skills and I knew that the University of Zurich had a very good reputation. Also, I wanted to explore the Swiss nature.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall, I had a very good experience. The university was great, the professors too and I lived with amazing people from all over the world.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was super easy, the departmental coordinators from UZH did an amazing job in providing the exchange students with all necessary information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received information about the university, the city and the different student offers.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was very lucky and was offered a place to stay through the university. A couple of months before arrival, I received an e-mail suggesting us to sign up for a list of housing. I would recommend everyone to do the same, because finding a place to live in Zurich seems almost impossible on your own.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you sign up for the list as before mentioned, you are pretty sure to get recomondation (although not 100% sure). Then you will receive an e-mail offering a housing opportunity, provided through WOKO (Student Housing Cooperative). The different housing opportunities range from smaller WG's (shared flats) to bigger dorms - many of them close to the city center and the different campuses (usually no more than 30 minutes away), and they are quite affordable - I even paid less here than in Copenhagen. There are no options for staying on campus, so I would strongly suggest you to accept the offer once you get it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The dorm did not offer the best facilities (we shared the kitchen with too many people) but the rooms were nice and I got to learn many new people - so it was definitely worth it.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a really great process. Of course it is always a bit challenging to navigate in a new system, but the departmental coordinators of UZH gave us the opportunity to pre sign up for course enrollment. So we could basically be ensured that we would get all the courses we wanted - really a great option.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I had a lot of contact back and forth with the coordinators, and they were always super helpful and usually replied in one or two days.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: As described before, I could get all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do a proper research before course enrollment. I could only take seminars with a lot of requirements during the semester and I would maybe have preferred to do some lectures too.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was quite high, but since I did the first semester of my masters here, I can only compare the level to the bachelor level in Copenhagen - so I guess the level must be equivalent to the level in Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was a bit different from Copenhagen and the style also varied in the different classes. But usually my classes were quite small and we had a lot of student interaction which I found really rewarding. We had a lot of activity during the semester, for example response papers and mid-terms. I was not really used to this, and sometimes it could be a bit stressful. But in the end it also gave me a lot of experience, so I am happy with the outcome.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Switzerland for Incomings (course for exchange students)
Globalization as a new challenge to global governance
Margaret Cavendish - Feminism, utopia or enlightenment
Post-Industrial Transformations: Cleavages, Policy and Politics
I also enrolled at two different German courses: One intensive course before the semester and one during the semester.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all of them! My professors were amazing and I have definitely gained a lot from taking the courses.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I paid 1200 DKK for a half-tax (a travel card that gives 50% discount on all travels in Switzerland). I also paid for the membership in the Opera. And then I just travelled a lot around in general.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything is expensive in Switzerland but it is definitely possible to save some money. Just do grocery shopping in cheaper places like Lidl or Aldi or eat in the canteen at uni. Buy the half-tax and month card if you want to travel a lot. The university offers a whole range of student sports (for free!) through the ASVZ community - so enjoy that. And you can get free entrance at many clubs on Thursdays (which is usually the party day of the week).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All sorts of sports (ASVZ!) and many different student associations. Also, the ESN (Erasmus Student Network) arranges a lot of different trips etc. You will receive all information about the different activities per mail from UZH.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Just do a lot of sports, it is so much fun and you can try anything there - the ASVZ system offered more than 100 different classes - ranging from football to sailing etc.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The Swiss nature is amazing, so please make use of it. We went on so many hikes and if you are into skiing, Switzerland is the place to be. Also, visit other cities, for example in the Italian or French parts of the country. Because of Switzerland's central location, it is super convenient to travel to places outside the country's borders, for example Germany or Italy. Zurich is a nice city also, where you can visit a lot of museums, swim in the Zurich lake or in the river, hike up the mountain Uetliberg, visit cafés or eat fondue or raclette (Swiss specialities).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty simple to be honest. (Most) Swiss people speak English very well and the infrastructure is great which makes it easy to get around. The Swiss people are not the most extroverted but they are always polite and willing to help.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to people in your class, do sports, sign up for a buddy through the mentor program (also provided by the university).

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Swiss people are always on time, so be sure to adapt or it will seem offensive.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The decency of Swiss people

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Explore the nature
2) Learn a bit of German
3) Bring money

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not hesitate to reach out to your professors - they were always really helpful.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in an international community, getting new friends from all over the world and practicing my academic English and German.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The courses were quite challenging in the beginning. But just focus on all the rewarding parts you get out of it.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: ENJOY!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
